name: Enable Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling (HAGS)
description: Lets the GPU manage its own work queue instead of the CPU-side scheduler.
mechanism: Sets HwSchMode=2 under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\GraphicsDrivers — the value behind Settings › Display › Graphics › 'Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling'. 1 = off, 2 = on.
benefit: Can slightly reduce CPU overhead and latency; it is required for NVIDIA DLSS Frame Generation.
drawback: Gains vary by game and driver (often within ±2%); some older drivers showed stutter or capture problems. Silently ignored when the GPU/driver does not support it.
recommendedFor: WDDM 2.7+ GPUs: NVIDIA GTX 10-series and newer, AMD RX 5000 and newer with current drivers, Intel Arc.
evidence: Microsoft DirectX Developer Blog, 'Hardware Accelerated GPU Scheduling' (2020). Verify after restart in Settings › Display › Graphics.

name: Disable Multiplane Overlay (troubleshooting only)
description: Turns off DWM multiplane overlays to work around flicker or stutter on some multi-monitor setups.
mechanism: Sets OverlayTestMode=5 under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\Dwm, which tells the Desktop Window Manager not to use hardware overlay planes.
benefit: Fixes flickering, black screens or periodic stutter caused by MPO driver bugs in specific configurations.
drawback: Disables a feature that normally saves power and can lower latency. Not a performance tweak — only use it if you have the symptoms. Recent Windows 11 builds may ignore this value.
evidence: Published by NVIDIA as a troubleshooting step (NVIDIA support article 5157, 2022).
